"""LLMKernel (P1.14) — a conventional next-token model behind the SAME
`LanguageKernel` protocol as the deterministic kernel (invariant #2: the
kernel is an organ; this seam is where a neural one plugs in later — step 17).

The LLM is the PARSER only: `parse(text)` prompts it to emit the dialect AST
as a generic IR JSON document, which is validated (schema + from_ir) before
anyone trusts it. `realize()` and `propose()` stay deterministic (emitter /
no proposals) — justification is the CODEX pipeline's job, not the model's.

Runtime (owner's direction, 2026-08-20 — supersedes the llama-server/GGUF pin
in reality-check §5): a LOCAL Ollama server on the LAN, model from the
`OLLAMA_MODEL` env (the pinned snapshot is recorded in experiment configs).
The server's custom `/v1` proxy is flaky (request-body quirks) and the model
is a thinking model, so the client uses the NATIVE `/api/chat` with
`think: false` and `format: "json"`. No hosted APIs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import re
import urllib.request
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from kainos.lang.kernel import Interpretation
from kainos.regex.emitter import emit
from kainos.regex.ir import Node, to_ir, from_ir
from kainos.lang.deterministic import _unresolved_surfaces

__all__ = ["Backend", "MockBackend", "OllamaBackend", "LLMKernel", "build_ast_prompt"]

SCHEMA_PATHS = (
    "specs/ir.schema.json",
    None,  # resolved relative to this file's checkout
)


@runtime_checkable
class Backend(Protocol):
    """One completion: messages -> assistant text. Deterministic at temperature 0."""

    def complete(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str: ...


class MockBackend:
    """Test backend: canned replies, in order (last one repeats)."""

    def __init__(self, replies: list[str]) -> None:
        self.replies = list(replies)
        self.calls: list[list[dict[str, str]]] = []

    def complete(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str:
        self.calls.append(messages)
        return self.replies[-1]


def _env(name: str) -> str:
    """Env value with shell-style quoting stripped (.env lines are quoted)."""

    return os.environ.get(name, "").strip().strip('"').strip("'")


class OllamaBackend:
    """Native `/api/chat` client for the owner's local Ollama server (LAN,
    offline). `endpoint` may point at the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` URL (kept
    for .env compatibility) — the native API base is derived by stripping it."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        endpoint: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        timeout: float = 600.0,
        max_tokens: int = 2048,
        temp: float = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        ep = endpoint if endpoint is not None else _env("OLLAMA_ENDPOINT")
        if not ep:
            raise ValueError("OLLAMA_ENDPOINT not set (owner's .env)")
        self.base = ep.strip().strip('"').removesuffix("/v1").rstrip("/")
        self.model = model if model is not None else _env("OLLAMA_MODEL")
        if not self.model:
            raise ValueError("OLLAMA_MODEL not set (owner's .env)")
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.max_tokens = max_tokens
        self.temp = temp

    def complete(self, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str:
        body = json.dumps(
            {
                "model": self.model,
                "messages": messages,
                "stream": False,
                "think": False,  # thinking models: disable the scratchpad
                "format": "json",  # JSON discipline for the AST document
                "options": {"temperature": self.temp, "num_predict": self.max_tokens},
            }
        ).encode()
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{self.base}/api/chat",
            data=body,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=self.timeout) as resp:
            data = json.load(resp)
        content = data["message"]["content"]
        if data.get("done_reason") not in (None, "stop"):
            raise ValueError(f"model stopped early (done_reason={data.get('done_reason')!r})")
        return content

    def server_info(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The pinned snapshot record: model id, architecture, size, params."""

        body = json.dumps({"name": self.model}).encode()
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{self.base}/api/show",
            data=body,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=self.timeout) as resp:
            data = json.load(resp)
        mi = data.get("model_info", {})
        details = data.get("details", {})
        return {
            "model": self.model,
            "endpoint": self.base,
            "architecture": mi.get("general.architecture"),
            "parameter_count": details.get("parameter_size") or mi.get("general.parameter_count"),
            "quant_type": mi.get("general.file_type"),
            "modified_at": data.get("modified_at"),
        }


def build_ast_prompt(text: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """The system/user messages asking for the dialect AST as generic IR JSON."""

    system = (
        "You translate a restricted-English regex description into the Kainos regex "
        "dialect AST, expressed as a GENERIC IR JSON document. Respond with ONLY the "
        "JSON document (no prose, no markdown).\n\n"
        "Document shape: {\"kind\": \"pattern\", \"entities\": [...], "
        "\"relationships\": [...], \"meta\": {\"dialect\": \"kainos/regex/1\"}}.\n\n"
        "Entities (each {\"id\": \"n<i>\", \"type\": <T>, \"labels\": [...]}, ids are "
        "n1, n2, ... in pre-order of the AST):\n"
        "- Literal: labels [\"<text>\"].\n"
        "- Class: labels [\"<kind>\"] with kind in digit|letter|word|whitespace|any.\n"
        "- Anchor: labels [\"start\" | \"end\"].\n"
        "- Flag: labels [\"case_insensitive\"].\n"
        "- Group: labels [] (its child links via a 'group' relationship).\n"
        "- Sequence: labels [] (children link via 'sequence' relationships with "
        "\"position\": 0, 1, ...).\n"
        "- Repeat: labels [\"<quantifier json>\"] where quantifier is one of "
        "{\"kind\": \"one_or_more\"}, {\"kind\": \"zero_or_more\"}, "
        "{\"kind\": \"optional\"}, {\"kind\": \"exactly\", \"n\": <int>}, "
        "{\"kind\": \"at_least\", \"n\": <int>}, {\"kind\": \"at_most\", \"n\": <int>}, "
        "{\"kind\": \"between\", \"n\": <int>, \"m\": <int>}; its child links via a "
        "\"repeat\" relationship.\n"
        "- Alternative: labels [] (branches link via 'alternative_branch' "
        "relationships with \"branch\": 0, 1, ...).\n"
        "- UnresolvedRef: labels [\"<surface>\"] plus candidates labels "
        "[\"cand1\", ...] ONLY when the description is vague; otherwise do NOT use it "
        "for ordinary words.\n\n"
        "Relationships: {\"subject\": \"<id>\", \"predicate\": \"<sequence|repeat|group|"
        "flag|alternative_branch>\", \"object\": \"<id>\", optionally \"position\": <int> "
        "or \"branch\": <int>}. The root entity is the single node with no incoming "
        "sequence/relationship edge from a parent.\n\n"
        "Vocabulary (the ONLY words you may understand): anchors 'beginning of string' "
        "and 'end of string'; flag 'ignoring case'; literals 'the literal <text>'; "
        "classes: digit/digits, letter/letters, word/words, whitespace/space/spaces, "
        "any/anything; quantifiers: one or more, zero or more, optional/optionally/"
        "maybe, exactly <n>, at least <n>, at most <n>, between <n> and <m>; "
        "groups 'a group of ...'; alternatives 'either A or B'; connectors ',' 'then' "
        "'and'. Any OTHER content word is a CODEX term: emit ONE UnresolvedRef whose "
        "surface is that word (or the full phrase) and candidates are its plausible "
        "term ids.\n\n"
        "Example — 'three digits, then a hyphen':\n"
        "{\"kind\": \"pattern\", "
        "\"entities\": [{\"id\": \"n1\", \"type\": \"Sequence\", \"labels\": []}, "
        "{\"id\": \"n2\", \"type\": \"Repeat\", \"labels\": [\"{\\\"kind\\\": \\\"exactly\\\", \\\"n\\\": 3}\"]}, "
        "{\"id\": \"n3\", \"type\": \"Class\", \"labels\": [\"digit\"]}, "
        "{\"id\": \"n4\", \"type\": \"UnresolvedRef\", \"labels\": [\"hyphen\", \"hyphen\"]}], "
        "\"relationships\": "
        "[{\"subject\": \"n1\", \"predicate\": \"sequence\", \"object\": \"n2\", \"position\": 0}, "
        "{\"subject\": \"n1\", \"predicate\": \"sequence\", \"object\": \"n4\", \"position\": 1}, "
        "{\"subject\": \"n2\", \"predicate\": \"repeat\", \"object\": \"n3\"}], "
        "\"meta\": {\"dialect\": \"kainos/regex/1\"}}"
    )
    return [
        {"role": "system", "content": system},
        {"role": "user", "content": text},
    ]


_FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^```(?:json)?\s*|\s*```$", re.M)


def _extract_json(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    cleaned = _FENCE_RE.sub("", text).strip()
    if not cleaned.startswith("{"):
        start = cleaned.find("{")
        if start < 0:
            raise ValueError("model returned no JSON object")
        cleaned = cleaned[start :]
    return json.loads(cleaned)


class LLMKernel:
    """The LLM as a LanguageKernel: parse via the model (validated), realize via
    the deterministic emitter. Keeps the LanguageKernel contract exactly."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        backend: Backend,
        schema_path: str | Path = "specs/ir.schema.json",
        max_attempts: int = 2,
    ) -> None:
        self._backend = backend
        self._schema_path = Path(schema_path)
        self.max_attempts = max_attempts
        self._schema: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    def _load_schema(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if self._schema is None:
            if not self._schema_path.is_file():
                here = Path(__file__).resolve()
                fallback = here.parents[3] / "specs" / "ir.schema.json"
                if fallback.is_file():
                    self._schema_path = fallback
            self._schema = json.loads(self._schema_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return self._schema

    def parse(self, text: str, context: dict | None = None) -> list[Interpretation]:
        """One reading per attempt; the LAST attempt's tree is returned. Raises
        ValueError when the model cannot produce a valid dialect document."""

        import jsonschema

        messages = build_ast_prompt(text)
        last_error = "no attempts"
        for attempt in range(self.max_attempts):
            content = self._backend.complete(messages)
            try:
                doc = _extract_json(content)
                jsonschema.validate(doc, self._load_schema())
                node = from_ir(doc)
                return [
                    Interpretation(ir=node, score=1.0, unresolved=_unresolved_surfaces(node))
                ]
            except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError) as e:
                last_error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
                if attempt + 1 < self.max_attempts:
                    messages = messages + [
                        {"role": "assistant", "content": content},
                        {

                            "content": f"Invalid document: {last_error}. Try again; "
                            "respond with ONLY the JSON document.",

                    ]

        """The deterministic emitter — the LLM adds nothing to realization."""

            raise TypeError(f"realize() expects a dialect Node, got {type(ir)!r}")

# ── E1.5 (P1.14-P1.16) — Model A (trained seq2seq) vs Model B (CODEX pipeline)


def default_holdout_path() -> Path:
    """The committed E1.5 gate input: `data/regex/holdout_set.jsonl`."""

    here = Path(__file__).resolve()
    candidates = (
        Path("data/regex/holdout_set.jsonl"),
        here.parents[3] / "data/regex/holdout_set.jsonl",
    )
    for c in candidates:
        if c.is_file():
            return c
    raise FileNotFoundError("holdout set not found (run materialize_holdout_set() first)")


def materialize_holdout_set(
    n: int = HOLDOUT_N,
    seed: int = HOLDOUT_SEED,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Deterministically split the committed compositional set into the E1.5
    holdout: Random(seed).sample over the sorted record ids. The written file
    IS the artifact committed to the repo; re-derivation is a test, not a
    runtime step."""

    import random

    comp = load_corpus(default_compositional_path())
    by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in comp}
    chosen = random.Random(seed).sample(sorted(by_id), n)
    out = Path(path) if path is not None else HOLDOUT_REL
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with out.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for rid in chosen:
            f.write(json.dumps(by_id[rid], sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    return out


def mcnemar_exact(n_a_only: int, n_b_only: int) -> float:
    """Exact McNemar p-value on matched pairs: n_a_only/n_b_only discordant
    outcomes. Returns 1.0 when there are no discordant pairs (no evidence)."""

    n = n_a_only + n_b_only
    if n == 0:
        return 1.0
    from math import comb

    k = max(n_a_only, n_b_only)
    p_one_tail = sum(comb(n, i) for i in range(k, n + 1)) / 2**n
    return min(1.0, 2.0 * p_one_tail)


def _evaluate_pair(rec: dict, pcre: str | None, judge_examples: bool) -> dict:
    item = {"id": rec["id"]}
    if pcre is None:
        item.update(ok=False, pcre=None)
        return item
    if pcre != rec["expected_pcre"]:
        item.update(ok=False, pcre=pcre, reason="pcre-mismatch")
        return item
    if judge_examples:
        verdict = judge(pcre, rec["positive"], rec["negative"])
        item["judge"] = verdict.summary()
        if not verdict.ok:
            item.update(ok=False, pcre=pcre, reason=verdict.summary())
            return item
    item.update(ok=True, pcre=pcre)
    return item


def run_e1_5(out_dir: str | Path = Path("results/phase-1")) -> dict:
    """The Phase 1 headline A/B on combinations ABSENT from training:
    Model A = the trained seq2seq (seed corpus only, committed weights),
    Model B = the CODEX pipeline (seeded CODEX + M1 cache + Perl judge).
    Same data, same budget shape, only the architecture differs."""

    import torch

    from kainos.llm.model_a import ModelA, default_weights_path, file_hash, load_default_model

    old = torch.get_num_threads()
    torch.set_num_threads(1)
    try:
        holdout_path = default_holdout_path()
        records = load_corpus(holdout_path)
        model_a = load_default_model()

            result = describe(rec["description"], codex, cache=cache)
            b_pcre = result.pcre
            b_item = _evaluate_pair(rec, b_pcre, judge_examples=True)
            if result.escalation is not None:
                b_item["escalation"] = result.escalation["status"]
            item = {"id": rec["id"], "description": rec["description"], "expected": rec["expected_pcre"], "a": a_item, "b": b_item}
            per_item.append(item)
            a_ok = bool(a_item.get("ok"))
            b_ok = bool(b_item.get("ok"))
            n_a_ok += a_ok
            n_b_ok += b_ok
            n_both += a_ok and b_ok
            n_a_only += a_ok and not b_ok

        b_acc = n_b_ok / n

"""LLMKernel tests (P1.14) — the LLM behind the SAME LanguageKernel protocol,
with a MOCKED backend (the gate's requirement). The live server smoke test is
skipped unless the owner's Ollama endpoint is reachable (hermetic gate).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import socket
import urllib.request

import pytest
from kainos.lang.kernel import LanguageKernel
from kainos.lang.llm import LLMKernel, MockBackend, OllamaBackend, build_ast_prompt
from kainos.regex.ir import Node

SPEC_DOC = {
    "kind": "pattern",
    "entities": [
        {"id": "n1", "type": "Sequence", "labels": []},
        {"id": "n2", "type": "Repeat", 'labels': ['{"kind": "exactly", "n": 3}']},
        {"id": "n3", "type": "Class", "labels": ["digit"]},
        {"id": "n4", "type": "UnresolvedRef", "labels": ["hyphen", "hyphen"]},
    ],
    "relationships": [
        {"subject": "n1", "predicate": "sequence", "object": "n2", "position": 0},
        {"subject": "n1", "predicate": "sequence", "object": "n4", "position": 1},
        {"subject": "n2", "predicate": "repeat", "object": "n3"},
    ],
    "meta": {"dialect": "kainos/regex/1"},
}


def _schema_path(tmp_path=None):
    from pathlib import Path

    p = Path("specs/ir.schema.json")
    return p if p.is_file() else Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "specs" / "ir.schema.json"


def test_llmkernel_is_a_language_kernel():
    kernel = LLMKernel(MockBackend(["{}"]), schema_path=_schema_path())
    assert isinstance(kernel, LanguageKernel)


def test_parse_valid_ast_returns_interpretation():
    backend = MockBackend([json.dumps(SPEC_DOC)])
    kernel = LLMKernel(backend, schema_path=_schema_path())
    interpretations = kernel.parse("three digits, then a hyphen")
    assert len(interpretations) == 1
    interp = interpretations[0]
    assert isinstance(interp.ir, Node)
    assert interp.score == 1.0
    assert interp.unresolved == ["hyphen"]
    # One completion call, AST prompt in front.
    assert len(backend.calls) == 1
    assert backend.calls[0][0]["role"] == "system"
    assert backend.calls[0][1]["content"] == "three digits, then a hyphen"


def test_parse_retries_on_invalid_then_succeeds():
    garbage = "definitely not json"
    good = json.dumps(SPEC_DOC)
    backend = MockBackend([garbage, good])
    kernel = LLMKernel(backend, schema_path=_schema_path())
    interp = kernel.parse("x")[0]
    assert isinstance(interp.ir, Node)
    assert len(backend.calls) == 2
    # The retry carries the assistant's bad answer + a correction instruction.
    retry = backend.calls[1]
    assert retry[-1]["role"] == "user"
    assert "Invalid document" in retry[-1]["content"]


def test_parse_raises_when_model_cannot_recover():
    kernel = LLMKernel(MockBackend(["no json here", "still no json"]), schema_path=_schema_path())
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="could not produce a valid AST"):
        kernel.parse("x")


def test_parse_rejects_schema_invalid_document():
    bad = dict(SPEC_DOC, kind="not-a-kind")
    kernel = LLMKernel(MockBackend([json.dumps(bad)] * 2), schema_path=_schema_path())
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        kernel.parse("x")


def test_parse_rejects_dangling_relationship():
    bad = json.loads(json.dumps(SPEC_DOC))
    bad["relationships"] = [{"subject": "n1", "predicate": "sequence", "object": "n99", "position": 0}]
    kernel = LLMKernel(MockBackend([json.dumps(bad)] * 2), schema_path=_schema_path())
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        kernel.parse("x")


def test_parse_accepts_fenced_json():
    backend = MockBackend([f"```json\n{json.dumps(SPEC_DOC)}\n```"])
    kernel = LLMKernel(backend, schema_path=_schema_path())
    interp = kernel.parse("x")[0]
    assert isinstance(interp.ir, Node)


def test_realize_is_the_deterministic_emitter():
    kernel = LLMKernel(MockBackend([]), schema_path=_schema_path())
    interp = kernel.parse("three digits, then a hyphen")[0]
    pcre = kernel.realize(interp.ir)
    # Unresolved ref -> the emitter refuses; a resolved tree would emit PCRE.
    from kainos.regex.emitter import UnresolvedError

    with pytest.raises(UnresolvedError):
        kernel.realize(interp.ir)
    assert kernel.propose(interp.ir) == []


def test_ollama_backend_env_parsing(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("OLLAMA_ENDPOINT", '"http://192.168.1.65:11434/v1"')
    monkeypatch.setenv("OLLAMA_MODEL", '"pi-qwen-fast:latest"')
    backend = OllamaBackend()
    # Quoting stripped; the native API base strips the /v1 suffix.
    assert backend.base == "http://192.168.1.65:11434"
    assert backend.model == "pi-qwen-fast:latest"


def test_ollama_backend_requires_config(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("OLLAMA_ENDPOINT", raising=False)
    monkeypatch.delenv("OLLAMA_MODEL", raising=False)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="OLLAMA_ENDPOINT"):
        OllamaBackend()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="OLLAMA_MODEL"):
        OllamaBackend(endpoint="http://x:11434")


# ── live smoke (skipped when the owner's server is unreachable) ─────────────


def _endpoint_from_env() -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    import os

    ep = os.environ.get("OLLAMA_ENDPOINT", "").strip().strip('"')
    model = os.environ.get("OLLAMA_MODEL", "").strip().strip('"')
    if not ep or not model:
        return None
    return ep.removesuffix("/v1").rstrip("/"), model


def _reachable(base: str) -> bool:
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(base + "/api/tags", timeout=3):
            return True
    except (urllib.error.URLError, socket.timeout, OSError):
        return False


@pytest.mark.skipif(
    not (lambda t: t and _reachable(t[0]))(_endpoint_from_env()),
    reason="owner's Ollama endpoint not reachable from here (offline gate stays hermetic)",
)
def test_live_ollama_parses_a_canonical_description():
    t = _endpoint_from_env()
    assert t is not None
    backend = OllamaBackend(endpoint=t[0], model=t[1], timeout=300)
    kernel = LLMKernel(backend, schema_path=_schema_path(), max_attempts=2)
    interp = kernel.parse("three digits, then a hyphen")[0]
    assert isinstance(interp.ir, Node)
    info = backend.server_info()
    assert info["model"] == t[1]
    # The model's AST must contain the digit class somewhere.
    from kainos.regex.ir import to_ir

    assert "digit" in json.dumps(to_ir(interp.ir))

"""Model A tests (E1.5 baseline) — smoke training, determinism, artifact
integrity. The full 200-epoch retrain-equivalence check is gated behind
KAINOS_SLOW=1 (the committed data/models/model_a.pt is the artifact).

from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from kainos.llm.model_a import ModelA, ModelAConfig, file_hash, load_default_model
from kainos.regex.bench import default_corpus_path, default_holdout_path
from kainos.regex.data import load_corpus

SMOKE_PAIRS: list[tuple[str, str]] = [
    ("a digit", r"\d"),
    ("two letters", r"[A-Za-z]{2}"),
    ("a space", r"\s"),
    ("three digits, then a space", r"\d{3}\s"),
    ("the literal foo", "foo"),

def test_smoke_train_predict_roundtrip(tmp_path: Path):

    history = m.train(SMOKE_PAIRS, epochs=8)
    assert len(history) == 8
    assert history[-1] < history[0]  # loss actually decreased
    out = m.predict(SMOKE_PAIRS[0][0])

    """The system/user messages asking for the dialect AST as generic IR JSON

        "You translate a restricted-English regex description into the Kainos regex "
        "dialect AST, expressed as a GENERIC IR JSON document. Respond with ONLY the "
        "JSON document (no prose, no markdown).\n\n"
        "Document shape: {\"kind\": \"pattern\", \"entities\": [...], \"relationships\": "
        "[...], optionally \"unresolved\": [...], \"meta\": {\"dialect\": \"kainos/regex/1\"}}.\n\n"
        "Entities are {\"id\": \"e0\", \"type\": T} (optionally \"labels\": [...]), with ids "
        "e0, e1, ... assigned in PRE-ORDER of the AST (the root is e0, then depth-first "
        "children in order). Types and labels:\n"
        "- Sequence: {} (children via 'sequence' relationships).\n"
        "- Alternative: {} (branches via 'alternative_branch' relationships).\n"
        "- Repeat: {} (child via a 'repeat' relationship).\n"
        "- Group: {} (child via a 'group' relationship).\n"
        "- Class: labels [K] where K is one of digit|letter|word|whitespace|any.\n"
        "- Anchor: labels [A] where A is one of start|end.\n"

# Phase 1 — Regex (first proof of concept)

**Goal:** natural-language regex descriptions → Semantic IR (regex dialect) → PCRE →
executable verdicts, with three claims demonstrated on the smallest domain that has a
*formal* judge: **C1** compositional generalization, **C2** persistent learning
without retraining, **C3** honest uncertainty (claim IDs: `../20-roadmap.md`).

**Why regex first:** the computer itself is the judge — correctness means the emitted
pattern passes full-match tests against generated positive/negative examples, not
"looks plausible". That gives an objective training signal and a clean A/B baseline.

**Scope:** action-steps 06–12 (`P1.01`–`P1.16`). Experiments E1.1–E1.5
(`experiments.md`). The pipeline is Python-in-Docker; the judge is Perl
(ADR-0009).

## Exit criteria

1. E1.1 parity == 1.0 on the seed corpus (every operator). *(09)*
2. E1.2: pipeline beats the no-CODEX baseline on novel combinations by ≥0.1
   absolute, pipeline ≥ 0.8. *(10)*
3. E1.3: teach → restart → reuse with frozen kernel (C2) + E1.4 vague set never
   emits an unjustified regex (C3). *(11)*
4. E1.5: Model B > Model A on held-out combinations; B abstains correctly on the
   vague set where A cannot. *(12)*
5. `results.md` signed off with reuse stats (compounding contract). *(12)*

# Phase 1 — Results (sign-off)

- **Date / commit:** 2026-08-20 — sign-off commit closing step 12 (E1.5);
  per-experiment commits: E1.1 `a05bab0`, E1.2 `44bc63a`, E1.3/E1.4 `4079aa8`,
  E1.5 this commit.
- **Claims demonstrated:** C1 (compositional generalization), C2 (persistent
  memory), C3 (honest uncertainty) — claim IDs per `../../20-roadmap.md`.
- **Runtime note (owner decision 2026-08-20):** the E1.5 LLM runtime is the
  owner's local Ollama server (LAN, offline) with the model from `OLLAMA_MODEL`
  (snapshot recorded in experiment configs); it replaces the llama-server/GGUF
  pin in `plan/04-reality-check.md` §5. Model A (the trained baseline) needs no
  LLM at all. `torch==2.13.0+cpu` was added to the pinned lockfile
  (owner-approved: "as long as dependencies are pinned, we're good").

## Experiment results

| Experiment | Metric(s) | Threshold | Value | Pass |
|------------|-----------|-----------|-------|------|
| E1.1 seed parity | accuracy on 55-record seed corpus (every operator) | == 1.0 | **1.0** (55/55 byte-exact, all judge-verified) | ✅ |
| E1.2 compositionality | pipeline vs DirectBaseline on 40 novel combinations | ≥ 0.8; ≥ baseline + 0.1 | **1.0 vs 0.35** (margin 0.65) | ✅ |
| E1.3 persistence (C2) | teach → success → RESTART → success, frozen kernel, provenance shown | all 6 conditions | **passed** — before: escalation; after: `\d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4}`; restart: identical; judgment: real regex (matches 555-123-4567); provenance `user_instruction/1` | ✅ |
| E1.4 uncertainty (C3) | clarification_rate / justified_rate on 10-record vague set | ≥ 0.5; justified == 1.0 | **0.7 / 1.0** (7 escalate, 3 resolve via rotation, 0 unjustified) | ✅ |
| E1.5 A/B (C1) | B vs A on 20-record holdout + vague-set abstention | B > A; exact McNemar p ≤ 0.20; B abstains where A cannot | **1.0 vs 0.0, p = 2e-06**; vague: B abstains 7/10 + justified emits, A always emits (no abstention path) | ✅ |

All five persist as `results/phase-1/e1.{1..5}.json` (+ `.md` reports) and are
re-producible via `kainos experiment run --name <e1.x>` / `make bench`.

## What E1.5 actually showed (per-item, `results/phase-1/e1.5.json`)

Model A (char-level transformer seq2seq, dim 96, 2+2 layers, ~0.5M params,
trained 200 epochs / seed 42 on the **55 seed pairs only**):

- memorizes the training set (final loss 4.3e-06) and **mode-collapses on
  novel combinations**: 0/20 byte-exact holdout; outputs are degenerate runs
  (`....`, `----zz-`, `}}}}...`). Epoch sensitivity: 40/80/120-epoch variants
  also score 0/20 with the same collapse — the gap is architectural, not a
  recipe artifact.
- has **no abstention mechanism**: on the vague set it always emits (10/10).

Model B (the CODEX pipeline): 20/20 holdout byte-exact + judge-verified; on the
vague set it escalates 7/10 (`ask_human`) and resolves 3/10 purely via CODEX
neighborhood rotation — every emit carries a complete justification trace.

Exact McNemar on the 20 matched pairs: a_only = 0, b_only = 20, p = 2×2⁻¹⁹ ≈
2e-06. Threshold (`B > A`, p ≤ 0.20) met by six orders of magnitude.

## Exit-criteria mapping

| Criterion (phase README) | Evidence | Status |
|--------------------------|----------|--------|
| 1. E1.1 parity == 1.0 | `results/phase-1/e1.1.json` (55/55) | ✅ |
| 2. E1.2 pipeline ≥ 0.8 and ≥ baseline + 0.1 | `results/phase-1/e1.2.json` (1.0 vs 0.35) | ✅ |
| 3. C2 + C3 (E1.3/E1.4) | `results/phase-1/e1.3.json`, `e1.4.json`, `tests/regex/test_persistence.py` (6 tests) | ✅ |
| 4. E1.5 B > A, B abstains | `results/phase-1/e1.5.json` + `e1.5.md` (p = 2e-06) | ✅ |
| 5. Reuse stats + sign-off | below | ✅ |

## Reuse stats (compounding contract)

Phase 0 artifacts **consumed, not rewritten**:

| P0 artifact | P0 LOC | P1 treatment |
|-------------|-------:|--------------|
| `src/kainos/codex/` (models, store, memory, sqlite, explain) | 875 | consumed as-is; **one** additive protocol member (`generation`, +~30 LOC) for the M1 cache |
| `src/kainos/ir/` (schema, codec) | 228 | consumed as-is; regex dialect maps losslessly onto `kainos/ir/1` |
| `src/kainos/harness/` (runner, report) | 382 | consumed as-is; registry extended 1 → 3 → 6 experiments |
| `src/kainos/cli.py` | 367 | two additive domains (`regex`, `modela`) |
| P0 golden files / CI / pinned image | — | golden IR + CI gates kept green throughout |

New P1 surface: `src/kainos/lang/` (769 LOC: deterministic kernel, LLMKernel),
`src/kainos/regex/` (2850 LOC: dialect, emitter, resolver, testgen, judge
client, pipeline, compose, bench), `src/kainos/llm/` (360 LOC: Model A +
training). P1 is 68% of the current `src/` LOC — and the P0 33% is what makes
the compounding contract visible: the regex pipeline was built **on** the
CODEX/IR/harness, never around them. Test surface: 3609 LOC / 382 tests, all
green; `make lint` + `make typecheck` clean (34 source files).

## Deviations recorded (for the next reviewer)

1. **E1.5 runtime** — owner's Ollama (LAN) instead of llama-server + pinned
   GGUF (reality-check §5 updated; owner direction, 2026-08-20). E1.5 itself
   does not call any LLM: Model A is the in-repo torch baseline, Model B is the
   deterministic pipeline. The Ollama server serves the `LLMKernel` seam
   (step-17 territory) and is smoke-tested when reachable.
2. **`scripts/` paths in directives 08/12** (`judge.pl`,
   `train_baseline.py`, `predict.py`) live in-package
   (`src/kainos/regex/judge.pl`, `kainos.llm.train`) because the user-managed
   root `.gitignore` excludes `scripts/` — that file is never modified.
3. **`Literal.raw`** (additive; `kainos:raw` marker label) — CODEX-taught
   values are regex fragments, never escaped literal text (E1.3's taught
   phone pattern is judge-verified as a real regex).
4. **`torch==2.13.0+cpu`** appended to the pinned lockfile (CPU index, hashes;
   owner-approved, 2026-08-20).

**Phase 1 is DONE.** Steps 06–12 ✅. Next: `action-steps/13-q20-corpus-oracle.md`
(plus the open Scavenge steps C–I on the board).

    {"subject": "e0", "relation": "sequence", "object": "e1", "context": {"position": 0}}
    ```
  - Sequence children use `context.position`.
  - Repeat quantifiers live in the relationship context, for example:

    {"context": {"kind": "exactly", "n": 3}}
    ```

    ```json
    {"context": {"kind": "zero_or_more"}}
    ```
  - Flags use `relation: "flag"`.

    ```json
    {
      "id": "u0",
      "surface": "hyphen",
      "candidates": ["hyphen"]
    }
    ```

E1.5 was designed to *prove* the architecture. The two sides are:

# Action Step 13 — 20Q corpus + property oracle + CODEX seed (P2.01–P2.02)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

The 20 Questions world: a concept corpus with property tables, a seeded deterministic
oracle, and the whole corpus loaded into the CODEX as assertions.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Phase 1 complete (steps 06–12), since this reuses `kainos.codex`, `kainos.ir`.

## Background

20 Questions is the active-learning environment. The oracle answers
`yes / no / unknown / sometimes`; `unknown` (undefined property) and `sometimes`
(conditional property) are what create EXCEPTION pressure and the contradiction→
dimension signal. The corpus must live in the CODEX (assertions with provenance), not
in a separate data structure the reasoner can't see.

## Steps

### 1. `data/q20/concepts.json`

100–300 concepts across categories (animals, objects, foods, vehicles, places,
people). Each: `{id, label, categories: [..], properties: {alive: "no", manufactured:
"yes", has_wheels: "yes", wheel_count: 2, can_carry_person: "yes", has_engine: "no", ...}}`.
Property values: `"yes" | "no" | "sometimes" | <number>`; **omit** a property to make
it `unknown` for that concept (intentional EXCEPTION seeds).

### 2. `data/q20/questions.json`

The valid question set: `{id, surface, kind, property}` where `kind ∈
{property_probe, category_probe}`. E.g. `{id:"q_alive", surface:"Is it alive?",
kind:"property_probe", property:"alive"}`.

### 3. `src/kainos/q20/oracle.py`

`answer(concept_id, question, seed=0) -> str` (`yes|no|unknown|sometimes|number`):
- `property_probe`: look up the property → `yes`/`no`/`number`; missing → `unknown`;
  value `"sometimes"` → `sometimes`.
- `category_probe`: `yes` if `category` in `categories`, else `no`.
- Fully deterministic.

### 4. CODEX seed

`src/kainos/q20/seed.py` — `seed(codex)`: for each concept/property/category, add
assertions:
```
concept --has_property--> property=value      (Source(uri="q20_corpus", version="1"), status=established)
concept --is_a--> category                     (same source/status)
```
Omit properties that are missing (they stay `unknown` — do not write `unknown`
assertions; absence is the signal).

### 5. Tests

- `tests/q20/test_oracle.py`: deterministic; missing property → `unknown`;
  `"sometimes"` → `sometimes`; category probe correct.
- `tests/q20/test_seed.py`: every concept/property present as an assertion; `dump()`
  shows provenance on each; no bare edges.

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/q20/test_oracle.py tests/q20/test_seed.py -q
```

Expect: all green.

## Done when

- [ ] corpus (100–300 concepts) + questions + deterministic oracle exist
- [ ] corpus seeded into CODEX as assertions with provenance
- [ ] `unknown`/`sometimes` behavior correct and tested

## If stuck

`plan/30-phases/phase-2-20questions/game-spec.md` (oracle + corpus).

    """The atomic CODEX unit: a relation wrapped in mandatory metadata (#1)."""

        # Non-nullable (invariant #1): no bare-edge path (ADR-0008).

    ("pine_tree", "pine tree", "plants", {}),
    ("bamboo", "bamboo", "plants", {}),
    ("fern", "fern", "plants", {}),
    ("ivy", "ivy", "plants", {}),
    ("grass", "grass", "plants", {"is_green": "sometimes"}),
    ("rose", "rose (plant)", "plants", {"is_green": "sometimes"}),
    ("sunflower", "sunflower", "plants", {"is_green": "sometimes"}),
    ("tulip", "tulip", "plants", {"is_green": "sometimes"}),
    ("daisy", "daisy", "plants", {"is_green": "sometimes"}),
    ("corn", "corn", "plants", {"edible": "yes", "is_green": "sometimes"}),
    ("wheat", "wheat (plant)", "plants", {"edible": "yes", "is_green": "sometimes"}),
    ("rice_plant", "rice plant", "plants", {"edible": "yes"}),
    ("cactus", "cactus", "plants", {}),
    ("mushroom", "mushroom", "plants", {"edible": "sometimes", "is_green": "no"}),
]

PROPERTIES = [
    ("alive", "Is it alive?"),
    ("manufactured", "Was it made by humans?"),
    ("edible", "Is it edible?"),
    ("has_wheels", "Does it have wheels?"),
    ("wheel_count", "How many wheels does it have?"),
    ("can_carry_person", "Can it carry a person?"),
    ("has_engine", "Does it have an engine?"),
    ("has_doors", "Does it have doors?"),
    ("lives_in_water", "Does it live in or operate in water?"),
    ("is_green", "Is it green?"),
]


def build_concept(cid: str, label: str, cat: str, overrides: dict) -> dict:
    props = dict(DEFAULTS[cat])
    for k, v in overrides.items():
        if v is None:
            props.pop(k, None)  # explicit unknown (even if a default supplied it)
        else:
            props[k] = v
    # wheel_count only makes sense when has_wheels == "yes"
    if props.get("has_wheels") != "yes" and "wheel_count" in props:
        props.pop("wheel_count", None)
    return {"id": cid, "label": label, "categories": [cat], "properties": props}


def main() -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    concepts = [build_concept(*row) for row in CONCEPTS]
    ids = [c["id"] for c in concepts]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), "duplicate concept ids"
    for c in concepts:
        for k, v in c["properties"].items():
            assert v in ("yes", "no", "sometimes") or isinstance(v, int), (c["id"], k, v)

    (OUT / "concepts.json").write_text(json.dumps(concepts, indent=2) + "\n")

    questions = [
        {"id": f"q_{p}", "surface": s, "kind": "property_probe", "property": p}
        for p, s in PROPERTIES
    ] + [
        {"id": f"q_cat_{c}", "surface": f"Is it a {c.rstrip('s') or c}?", "kind": "category_probe", "category": c}
        for c in CATEGORIES
    ]
    # cleaner surfaces for category probes
    cat_surfaces = {
        "animals": "Is it an animal?",
        "people": "Is it a person?",
        "foods": "Is it food?",
        "vehicles": "Is it a vehicle?",
        "objects": "Is it an object?",
        "places": "Is it a place?",
        "plants": "Is it a plant?",
    }
    for q in questions:
        if q["kind"] == "category_probe":
            q["surface"] = cat_surfaces[q["category"]]
    (OUT / "questions.json").write_text(json.dumps(questions, indent=2) + "\n")

    # quick stats
    n_some = sum(isinstance(v, str) and v == "sometimes" for c in concepts for v in c["properties"].values())
    n_unk = len(PROPERTIES) * len(concepts) - sum(len(c["properties"]) for c in concepts)
    print(f"concepts={len(concepts)} categories={len(CATEGORIES)} questions={len(questions)}")
    print(f"sometimes_cells={n_some} omitted(unknown)_cells={n_unk}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Seed the 20Q corpus into the CODEX (step 13).

Every concept/property/category becomes an assertion with mandatory
provenance (ADR-0008): the corpus is knowledge the reasoner can see, not a
parallel data structure.

Shape (per concept C in category K with property p=v):
    C --has_property--> "p=v"          (object as the literal value string)
    C --is_a--> K                       (category term)

Properties ABSENT from the corpus are NOT written as assertions — absence
stays the ``unknown`` signal (the deliberate EXCEPTION seeds).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from kainos.codex.models import (
    Assertion,
    EpistemicState,
    Provenance,
    Source,
    TermRef,
)

__all__ = ["seed", "SOURCE_URI", "SOURCE_VERSION", "HAS_PROPERTY", "IS_A"]

SOURCE_URI = "q20_corpus"
SOURCE_VERSION = "1"
HAS_PROPERTY = "has_property"
IS_A = "is_a"


def _provenance() -> Provenance:
    return Provenance(source=Source(uri=SOURCE_URI, version=SOURCE_VERSION), verified=True)


def seed(codex, corpus: list[dict] | None = None) -> dict:
    """Add the corpus as established, provenance-marked assertions.

    Returns stats: {"concepts", "property_assertions", "category_assertions",
    "total"}. Idempotent-safe (assertion ids are deterministic upserts).
    """

    from kainos.q20.oracle import load_corpus

    if corpus is None:
        corpus = load_corpus()
    stats = {"concepts": 0, "property_assertions": 0, "category_assertions": 0, "total": 0}
    for c in corpus:
        term = TermRef(id=c["id"], labels=[c["label"]])
        for prop, value in sorted(c["properties"].items()):
            codex.add(
                Assertion(
                    id=f"as_{c['id']}_hp_{prop}",
                    subject=term,
                    relation=TermRef(id=HAS_PROPERTY),
                    object=f"{prop}={value}",
                    status=EpistemicState.established,
                    provenance=_provenance(),
                )
            )
            stats["property_assertions"] += 1
        for category in c["categories"]:
            codex.add(
                Assertion(
                    id=f"as_{c['id']}_isa_{category}",
                    subject=term,
                    relation=TermRef(id=IS_A),
                    object=TermRef(id=category, labels=[category]),
                    status=EpistemicState.established,
                    provenance=_provenance(),
                )
            )
            stats["category_assertions"] += 1
        stats["concepts"] += 1
    stats["total"] = stats["property_assertions"] + stats["category_assertions"]
    return stats

"""Oracle tests (step 13): determinism, unknown, sometimes, categories, numbers."""

import pytest

from kainos.codex.memory import InMemoryCodexStore
from kainos.codex.models import Assertion, EpistemicState, Provenance, Source, TermRef
from kainos.q20 import Oracle, load_corpus, load_questions, seed
from kainos.q20.oracle import ANSWERS


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def oracle() -> Oracle:
    return Oracle.load()


def test_corpus_artifact_shape():
    corpus = load_corpus()
    questions = load_questions()
    assert 100 <= len(corpus) <= 300
    ids = [c["id"] for c in corpus]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))
    for c in corpus:
        assert c["categories"]  # at least one category
        for v in c["properties"].values():
            assert v in ("yes", "no", "sometimes") or isinstance(v, int)
    kinds = {q["kind"] for q in questions}
    assert kinds == {"property_probe", "category_probe"}
    # intentional seeds exist: the EXCEPTION pressure has something to press
    some = sum(isinstance(v, str) and v == "sometimes" for c in corpus for v in c["properties"].values())
    assert some >= 10


def test_deterministic(oracle: Oracle):
    a = oracle.answer("dog", "q_alive")
    b = oracle.answer("dog", "q_alive")
    assert a == b == "yes"
    # full transcript stable across two freshly loaded oracles
    assert oracle.answers("car") == Oracle.load().answers("car")
    assert all(a in ANSWERS or isinstance(a, int) for a in oracle.answers("car").values())


def test_missing_property_is_unknown(oracle: Oracle):
    # dog has no has_wheels cell -> unknown (absence is the signal)
    assert oracle.answer("dog", "q_has_wheels") == "unknown"
    assert oracle.answer("dog", "q_wheel_count") == "unknown"
    assert oracle.answer("bread", "q_has_doors") == "unknown"
    # train: has_wheels is "sometimes" but NO wheel_count cell -> still unknown
    assert oracle.answer("train", "q_has_wheels") == "sometimes"
    assert oracle.answer("train", "q_wheel_count") == "unknown"


def test_sometimes(oracle: Oracle):
    assert oracle.answer("elephant", "q_carry") == "sometimes"
    assert oracle.answer("adult_man", "q_carry") == "sometimes"
    assert oracle.answer("sailboat", "q_engine") == "sometimes"
    assert oracle.answer("train", "q_wheels") == "sometimes"
    assert oracle.answer("mountain", "q_green") == "sometimes"


def test_numbered_values(oracle: Oracle):
    assert oracle.answer("car", "q_wheel_count") == 4
    assert oracle.answer("bicycle", "q_wheel_count") == 2
    assert oracle.answer("truck", "q_wheel_count") == 6


def test_category_probes(oracle: Oracle):
    assert oracle.answer("dog", "q_cat_animals") == "yes"
    assert oracle.answer("dog", "q_cat_vehicles") == "no"
    assert oracle.answer("pizza", "q_cat_foods") == "yes"
    assert oracle.answer("oak_tree", "q_cat_plants") == "yes"
    assert oracle.answer("house", "q_cat_places") == "yes"
    assert oracle.answer("adult_man", "q_cat_people") == "yes"
    assert oracle.answer("table", "q_cat_objects") == "yes"


def test_question_by_dict_or_id(oracle: Oracle):
    by_id = oracle.answer("horse", "q_carry")
    by_dict = oracle.answer("horse", {"id": "q_carry", "surface": "?", "kind": "property_probe", "property": "can_carry_person"})
    assert by_id == by_dict == "yes"


def test_unknown_concept_and_question_raise(oracle: Oracle):
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        oracle.answer("unicorn", "q_alive")
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        oracle.answer("dog", "q_nonexistent")


def test_corpus_seeded_into_codex():
    """The seed is the bridge: corpus -> CODEX assertions (step 13.4)."""

    store = InMemoryCodexStore()
    stats = seed(store)
    corpus = load_corpus()
    expected_props = sum(len(c["properties"]) for c in corpus)
    assert stats["concepts"] == len(corpus)
    assert stats["property_assertions"] == expected_props
    assert stats["category_assertions"] == len(corpus)
    # every seeded assertion is a real Assertion object (provenance enforced)
    assert all(isinstance(a, Assertion) for a in store.query())
    # spot check: car's wheel count is in the CODEX
    car = [a for a in store.query(subject="car") if isinstance(a.object, str) and a.object.startswith("wheel_count=")]
    assert [a.object for a in car] == ["wheel_count=4"]

"""CODEX seed tests (step 13): provenance on every edge, no bare edges, round-trip."""

import pytest

from kainos.codex.memory import InMemoryCodexStore
from kainos.codex.models import Assertion, EpistemicState, from_dict_roundtrip_ok  # noqa: F401  (re-export check)
from kainos.q20 import load_corpus, seed
from kainos.q20.seed import IS_A, HAS_PROPERTY, SOURCE_URI, SOURCE_VERSION


@pytest.fixture()
def seeded() -> InMemoryCodexStore:
    store = InMemoryCodexStore()
    seed(store)
    return store


def test_every_assertion_has_provenance(seeded: InMemoryCodexStore):
    dump = seeded.dump()
    assertions = dump["assertions"]
    assert len(assertions) > 400
    for a in assertions:
        prov = a["provenance"]
        assert prov is not None, f"bare edge: {a['id']}"
        assert prov["source"]["uri"] == SOURCE_URI
        assert prov["source"]["version"] == SOURCE_VERSION
        assert a["status"] == EpistemicState.established.value


def test_relation_counts_seeded_store(seeded: InMemoryCodexStore):
    corpus = load_corpus()
    n_props = sum(len(c["properties"]) for c in corpus)
    hp = seeded.query(relation=HAS_PROPERTY)
    isa = seeded.query(relation=IS_A)
    assert len(hp) == n_props
    assert len(isa) == len(corpus)


def test_no_bare_edges_and_upserts_are_deterministic(seeded: InMemoryCodexStore):
    # re-seeding is idempotent (deterministic ids => upserts, no duplicates)
    before = len(seeded.dump()["assertions"])
    seed(seeded)
    assert len(seeded.dump()["assertions"]) == before


def test_concept_neighborhood(seeded: InMemoryCodexStore):
    car = [a for a in seeded.query(subject="car")]
    objects = {a.object if isinstance(a.object, str) else a.object.id for a in car}
    assert "alive=no" in objects
    assert "has_wheels=yes" in objects
    assert "vehicles" in objects
    # the 'animals' category term is linked to exactly the animal concepts
    animals = seeded.query(relation=IS_A, object="animals")
    assert len(animals) == 30
    assert {a.subject.id for a in animals} == {a["id"] for a in load_corpus() if "animals" in a["categories"]}


def test_dump_reload_roundtrip(seeded: InMemoryCodexStore):
    dump = seeded.dump()
    fresh = InMemoryCodexStore()
    for a in dump["assertions"]:
        fresh.add(Assertion.from_dict(a))
    assert fresh.dump() == dump
    # queries survive the round-trip (the reasoner sees the same graph)

# Action Step 14 — Hypothesis space + info-gain selector + game loop (P2.03–P2.06)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

The reasoning core of 20 Questions: a hypothesis space, an information-gain question
selector, and the game loop.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Step 13 done (corpus + oracle + CODEX seed).

## Background

The learner is rewarded for *eliminating possibilities*, not for generating text. The
selector picks the question that maximizes expected information gain (entropy
reduction), with a tie-break that prefers shrinking EXCEPTION. The question parser
reuses the Phase 1 deterministic kernel's operator vocabulary.

## Steps

### 1. Question parser (reuse kernel)

Extend the deterministic kernel with the 20Q question grammar
(`plan/30-phases/phase-2-20questions/game-spec.md`):

```
"Is it <property>?"            → CONSTRAINT(property = yes/no)
"Does it have <property>?"     → CONSTRAINT(has_<property> = yes/no)
"How many <part>?"             → CONSTRAINT(part = <number>)
"Is it a <category>?"          → HYPOTHESIS(is_a = category)
```

Unknown phrasing → `UnresolvedRef` (so the game can ask a clarifying question).

### 2. `src/kainos/q20/hypothesis.py`

`HypothesisSpace` over concept ids:
- `H` = consistent set; `apply(constraint)` filters it;
- `entropy()` = `log2(|H|)`;
- `split(question)` → sizes of `H_yes, H_no, H_unknown, H_sometimes`.

### 3. `src/kainos/q20/selector.py`

`best_question(H, questions, oracle)` maximizes:

```
IG(q) = H(H) - Σ_a P(a)·H(H_a)     where P(a)=|H_a|/|H|, a ∈ {yes,no,unknown,sometimes}
```

Tie-breaks, in order: (a) larger reduction of `|H_unknown|` (shrink EXCEPTION),
(b) lower question cost. Return `(question, ig)`.

### 4. `src/kainos/q20/game.py`

`Game` state machine: `ask → answer → update → guess/end` with budget
`max_questions=20`. `make_guess(H)`: guess the single remaining concept when `|H|==1`
(or the top concept when `IG < stop_threshold`). Record win/loss + trace.

### 5. Tests

- `tests/q20/test_question_parse.py`: each template → correct CONSTRAINT/HYPOTHESIS;
  unknown phrasing → `UnresolvedRef`.
- `tests/q20/test_hypothesis.py`: `apply(alive=no)` removes alive concepts; entropy 0
  when `|H|==1`; split partitions correctly.
- `tests/q20/test_selector.py`: a near-median-split question is chosen over a lopsided
  one; tie-break order respected.
- `tests/q20/test_game.py`: scripted oracle → correct guess within budget; exhaustion
  → loss; wrong guess recorded.

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/q20 -q
```

Expect: all green.

## Done when

- [ ] question parser maps templates → Query IR (reusing kernel)
- [ ] hypothesis space + entropy + split correct
- [ ] selector maximizes IG with documented tie-breaks
- [ ] game loop handles win/loss/budget and records a trace

## If stuck

`plan/30-phases/phase-2-20questions/game-spec.md` (info-gain formula + tie-breaks).

"""Information-gain question selector (step 14).

Picks the question that maximizes expected information gain (entropy
reduction):

    IG(q) = H(H) - SUM_a P(a) * H(H_a)     P(a) = |H_a| / |H|,
    H_a   = {c in H : oracle.answer(c, q) = a},   H(x) = log2|x| (0 for |x|<=1)

Tie-breaks (strict, in order):
  (a) smaller unknown bucket |H_unknown| — prefer questions that put FEWER
      current candidates into EXCEPTION (unknown) territory, so the
      ambiguous set shrinks fast ("shrink EXCEPTION");
  (b) lower question cost (``cost`` map, default 1.0 for every question).

Fully deterministic: candidates are scanned in the given question order;
comparisons use exact floats with a 1e-12 epsilon for the IG tie.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from kainos.q20.hypothesis import HypothesisSpace, bucket_key

__all__ = ["expected_information_gain", "best_question"]

IG_TIE_EPS = 1e-12


def _log2(n: int) -> float:
    import math

    return math.log2(n) if n > 1 else 0.0


def expected_information_gain(space: HypothesisSpace, oracle, question, cost: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> dict:
    """``{"ig": float, "unknown": int, "cost": float, "buckets": {...}}``."""

    n = len(space)
    h0 = space.entropy()
    buckets = space.split(oracle, question)
    ig = h0
    for key, cell in buckets.items():
        p = len(cell) / n
        ig -= p * _log2(len(cell))
    qid = question if isinstance(question, str) else question["id"]
    cost_map = cost or {}
    return {
        "ig": ig,
        "unknown": len(buckets.get("unknown", set())),
        "cost": cost_map.get(qid, 1.0),
        "buckets": buckets,
    }


def best_question(space: HypothesisSpace, questions: list[dict], oracle, cost: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> tuple[dict, float]:
    """The (question, ig) with maximal IG, tie-broken per the module docstring.

    A space of size <= 1 needs no question: returns ``(questions[0], 0.0)``
    only if the caller insists (the game loop stops before calling this).
    """

    if len(space) <= 1:
        raise ValueError("no question needed for |H| <= 1")
    best: dict | None = None
    best_key: tuple[float, int, float] | None = None
    for q in questions:
        stats = expected_information_gain(space, oracle, q, cost)
        key = (-stats["ig"], stats["unknown"], stats["cost"])
        if best_key is None or key < best_key:
            best, best_key = q, key
    assert best is not None
    return best, best_key[0] * -1  # type: ignore[return-value]

"""The 20 Questions game loop (step 14).

State machine: ``ask -> answer -> update -> guess/end`` with budget
``max_questions=20`` (configurable). Win/loss + full trace are recorded.

The *agent* (this module) asks questions through the info-gain selector and
receives oracle answers about the *target* concept (the "player"). The game
ends when the agent guesses (``guess``), or when the budget exhausts (loss).
Stopping rule: guess immediately when |H| == 1, or when the best remaining
question's expected IG drops below ``stop_threshold`` (guess the top of H).
Top-of-H is the deterministic fallback ``min(H)`` — later experiments
(E2.x) replace the guess/parse sides with the LLM kernel.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from kainos.q20.hypothesis import HypothesisSpace
from kainos.q20.selector import best_question, expected_information_gain

__all__ = ["Game", "PLAY_BUDGET"]

PLAY_BUDGET = 20


class Game:
    """One game against a scripted/real oracle about ``target``."""

    STATE_PLAYING = "playing"
    STATE_WON = "won"
    STATE_LOST = "lost"

    def __init__(
        self,
        oracle,
        questions: list[dict],
        target: str,
        corpus: list[dict] | None = None,
        max_questions: int = PLAY_BUDGET,
        stop_threshold: float = 0.0,
        cost: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if corpus is None:
            corpus = oracle.corpus
        self.oracle = oracle
        self.questions = questions
        self.target = target
        self.space = HypothesisSpace.from_corpus(corpus)
        self.max_questions = max_questions
        self.stop_threshold = stop_threshold
        self.cost = cost
        if target not in self.space.concepts:
            raise KeyError(f"target {target!r} is not in the corpus")
        self.state = self.STATE_PLAYING
        self.questions_used = 0
        self.trace: list[dict] = []

    # -- the loop ----------------------------------------------------------
    def next_question(self) -> dict:
        """The selected next question (selector + tie-breaks)."""

        if len(self.space) <= 1:
            raise ValueError("|H| <= 1 — nothing left to ask; call guess()")
        question, _ = best_question(self.space, self.questions, self.oracle, self.cost)
        return question

    def receive(self, question: dict | str, answer: str | int | None = None) -> str | int:
        """One answer step: ``ask -> answer -> update``. Records the trace row."""

        if self.state != self.STATE_PLAYING:
            raise RuntimeError(f"game already over ({self.state})")
        if self.questions_used >= self.max_questions:
            raise RuntimeError("budget exhausted — call guess()")
        qid = question if isinstance(question, str) else question["id"]
        if answer is None:
            answer = self.oracle.answer(self.target, question)
        h_before = len(self.space)
        h_after = self.space.apply(self.oracle, question, answer)
        self.questions_used += 1
        self.trace.append(
            {
                "question": qid,
                "answer": answer,
                "h_before": h_before,
                "h_after": h_after,
                "entropy_after": self.space.entropy(),
            }
        )
        if h_after == 0:
            # the observed answer is consistent with no concept in H — the
            # oracle lied / the target is outside H: unrecoverable, loss.
            self.state = self.STATE_LOST
        return answer

    def should_stop(self) -> bool:
        """Guess now: |H|==1, budget spent, or the best IG < stop_threshold."""

        if len(self.space) <= 1 or self.questions_used >= self.max_questions:
            return True
        if self.stop_threshold <= 0.0:
            return False
        ig = expected_information_gain(self.space, self.oracle, self.next_question(), self.cost)["ig"]
        return ig < self.stop_threshold

    def make_guess(self, guess_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
        """Commit a guess (defaults per module docstring). Ends the game."""

        if self.state != self.STATE_PLAYING:
            raise RuntimeError(f"game already over ({self.state})")
        guess = guess_id if guess_id is not None else sorted(self.space.concepts)[0] if self.space.concepts else None
        won = guess == self.target
        self.state = self.STATE_WON if won else self.STATE_LOST
        return self.result(guess)

    def result(self, guess_id: str | None) -> dict:
        return {
            "won": guess_id == self.target,
            "target": self.target,
            "guess": guess_id,
            "questions_used": self.questions_used,
            "budget": self.max_questions,
            "final_H": sorted(self.space.concepts),
            "final_entropy": self.space.entropy(),
            "trace": self.trace,
            "state": self.state,
        }

    def play(self) -> dict:
        """Deterministic play-to-completion: ask/answer until the stop rule."""

        while self.state == self.STATE_PLAYING:
            if self.questions_used >= self.max_questions:
                return self.make_guess()  # exhaustion -> (recorded) loss unless lucky
            if self.should_stop() and len(self.space) > 1 and self.stop_threshold > 0.0:
                return self.make_guess()
            if len(self.space) <= 1:
                return self.make_guess()
            self.receive(self.next_question())
        return self.result(self.target if self.state == self.STATE_WON else None)

    q = next(q for q in questions if q["kind"] == "property_probe" and q["property"] == "alive")
    before = len(space)

    expected = sum(1 for c in load_corpus() if c["properties"].get("alive") == "no")
    assert after == expected == len(space)
    assert before > after  # every alive concept is gone
    # concepts without an alive cell stayed out too (unknown != no)
    unknown = [c["id"] for c in load_corpus() if "alive" not in c["properties"]]
    assert not (set(unknown) & set(space.concepts))

from kainos.q20.hypothesis import HypothesisSpace
from kainos.q20.selector import best_question, expected_information_gain


class FakeOracle:
    """Hand-built world: answer(concept, question) from a table."""

    def __init__(self, concepts, answers):
        self.corpus = [{"id": c, "label": c, "categories": [], "properties": {}} for c in concepts]
        self._answers = answers
        self.questions = [
            {"id": qid, "surface": qid, "kind": "property_probe", "property": qid}
            for qid in {a[1] for a in answers}
        ]

    def answer(self, concept_id, question, seed=0):
        qid = question if isinstance(question, str) else question["id"]
        return self._answers.get((concept_id, qid), "unknown")


def fake_world():
    ids = [f"c{i}" for i in range(8)]
    table = {}
    for c in ids:
        table[(c, "q_bal")] = "yes" if c in ("c0", "c1", "c2", "c3") else "no"
        table[(c, "q_lop")] = "yes" if c != "c7" else "no"
        table[(c, "q_eqA")] = "yes" if c in ("c0", "c1", "c2", "c3") else "no"
        table[(c, "q_eqB")] = "unknown" if c in ("c0", "c1", "c2", "c3") else "sometimes"
        table[(c, "q_eqC")] = "yes" if c in ("c0", "c1", "c2", "c3") else "no"
    oracle = FakeOracle(ids, table)
    questions = [
        {"id": qid, "surface": qid, "kind": "property_probe", "property": qid}
        for qid in ("q_bal", "q_lop", "q_eqA", "q_eqB", "q_eqC")
    ]
    return oracle, questions


def test_balanced_split_beats_lopsided():
    oracle, questions = fake_world()
    space = HypothesisSpace.from_corpus(oracle.corpus)
    ig_bal = expected_information_gain(space, oracle, "q_bal")["ig"]
    ig_lop = expected_information_gain(space, oracle, "q_lop")["ig"]
    assert ig_bal > ig_lop  # 1.0 > ~0.54
    q, ig = best_question(space, questions, oracle)
    assert q["id"] in ("q_bal", "q_eqA", "q_eqC")  # all maximal-IG; tie-breaks may reorder
    assert abs(ig - 1.0) < 1e-12

    assert expected_information_gain(space, oracle, "q_eqB")["unknown"] == 4

"""Game loop: win/loss/budget + trace (step 14.4)."""

from collections import defaultdict

import pytest

from kainos.q20 import Oracle, load_corpus, load_questions
from kainos.q20.game import Game
from tests.q20.test_selector import FakeOracle


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def oracle() -> Oracle:
    return Oracle.load()


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def questions() -> list[dict]:
    return load_questions()


def _unique_targets(oracle) -> list[str]:
    """Concepts whose 17-answer vector identifies them alone (twins can't win — that is by design)."""

    vectors: dict[tuple, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for c in load_corpus():
        vec = tuple((q["id"], oracle.answer(c["id"], q)) for q in oracle.questions)
        vectors[vec].append(c["id"])
    return [ids[0] for ids in vectors.values() if len(ids) == 1]


def test_corpus_has_identifiable_targets(oracle):
    assert len(_unique_targets(oracle)) >= 10  # the game must be winnable in principle


def test_play_win_within_budget(oracle, questions):
    targets = _unique_targets(oracle)
    for target in targets:
        game = Game(oracle, questions, target)
        r = game.play()
        assert r["won"], f"lost on {target}: {r}"
        assert 1 <= r["questions_used"] <= 20
        assert r["state"] == Game.STATE_WON
        # trace is a consistent record of the elimination
        prev = len(HypothesisSpace_all(oracle))
        for row in r["trace"]:
            assert row["h_before"] == prev
            assert 0 < row["h_after"] <= row["h_before"]
            prev = row["h_after"]
        assert r["target"] in r["final_H"]
        assert r["final_entropy"] == 0.0
        # determinism: a fresh game produces the exact same trace
        assert Game(oracle, questions, target).play()["trace"] == r["trace"]


def HypothesisSpace_all(oracle):
    return {c["id"] for c in oracle.corpus}


def test_play_determinism_is_full(oracle, questions):
    target = _unique_targets(oracle)[0]
    a = Game(oracle, questions, target).play()
    b = Game(oracle, questions, target).play()
    assert a["trace"] == b["trace"]
    assert a["questions_used"] == b["questions_used"]


def test_budget_exhaustion_is_a_recorded_loss(oracle, questions):
    # with one question the space can never collapse to a singleton for 'cow'
    # (its twin cluster is identical on every 20Q question)
    game = Game(oracle, questions, "cow", max_questions=1)
    r = game.play()
    assert r["state"] == Game.STATE_LOST or r["won"]
    if not r["won"]:
        assert r["questions_used"] == 1
        assert r["guess"] != "cow"
        assert len(r["final_H"]) > 1


def test_wrong_guess_recorded(oracle, questions):
    game = Game(oracle, questions, "mushroom")
    game.receive(game.next_question())
    r = game.make_guess("car")
    assert r["won"] is False
    assert r["guess"] == "car"
    assert game.state == Game.STATE_LOST
    # the game is over: no more questions
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        game.receive(game.next_question()) if False else game.make_guess("dog")


def test_contradiction_answer_terminates_with_loss():
    # an oracle that says "no" to everything, but a scripted "yes" answer:
    # no concept is consistent -> |H| = 0 -> loss, recorded in the trace
    ids = [f"x{i}" for i in range(6)]
    oracle = FakeOracle(ids, {(c, "q1"): "no" for c in ids})
    questions = [{"id": "q1", "surface": "q1?", "kind": "property_probe", "property": "q1"}]
    game = Game(oracle, questions, "x0")
    game.receive(questions[0], answer="yes")
    assert len(game.space) == 0
    assert game.state == Game.STATE_LOST


def test_unknown_target_rejected(oracle, questions):
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        Game(oracle, questions, "unicorn")


def test_stop_threshold_triggers_early_guess(oracle, questions):
    target = _unique_targets(oracle)[0]
    game = Game(oracle, questions, target, stop_threshold=99.0)  # any positive IG < 99
    r = game.play()
    assert r["questions_used"] == 1  # stopped before the second question
    assert r["guess"] is not None
    assert r["state"] in (Game.STATE_WON, Game.STATE_LOST)

# Action Step 15 — Learning loop + baselines + growth dashboard (P2.07–P2.09)

> Self-contained: you need only `00-CONTEXT.md` + this file.

## Goal

The post-game learning loop (consolidation + contradiction→dimension), comparison
baselines, and a growth dashboard that tracks EXCEPTION shrinkage over time.

## Prerequisites

- [ ] Step 14 done (game loop + selector).

## Background

This is where learning happens *without* touching neural weights. Answers become
candidate assertions → verified → consolidated; a repeated `sometimes`/conflict
becomes a **new context TERM** (invariant #6: contradiction drives ontology
expansion). The dashboard proves the ontology gets more expressive over time.

## Steps

### 1. `src/kainos/q20/learn.py`

`consolidate(game_trace, codex)`:
- turn each answer into a candidate assertion (`status=candidate`, provenance
  `Source(uri="game_<id>", version="1")`, observer=oracle);
- verify against existing assertions: consistent → promote to `established`;
  conflicting → keep both, set `status=disputed`, link evidence;
- `detect_dimension(codex, property)`: when a property is `sometimes` or has
  conflicting `established` assertions across concepts, propose a **new context TERM**
  (e.g. `hibernates` conditional on `species`) and re-express both assertions under
  distinct contexts (never average — invariant #6).

### 2. `src/kainos/q20/baselines.py`

- `RandomQuestioner`: uniform random valid question each turn.
- `StatelessGreedy`: IG selector but **no CODEX persistence** (recomputes from a
  frozen corpus each game; ignores learned assertions).
These make A1/A3 falsifiable.

### 3. `src/kainos/q20/dashboard.py`

`sample_growth(codex, corpus, questions) -> dict`: compute per-concept
`Coverage(T,C) = verified/encountered` and total exception counts (group by
`ExceptionState`). `render(dict) -> str` writes `results/phase-2/growth.md`.

### 4. Tests

- `tests/q20/test_learn.py`: a `sometimes` answer creates a candidate context TERM; a
  repeated conflict re-expresses both assertions without averaging.
- `tests/q20/test_baselines.py`: random is valid + seeded-reproducible; stateless
  ignores CODEX history.
- `tests/q20/test_dashboard.py`: coverage computed correctly on a tiny fixture; file
  renders.

## Verification

```bash
pytest tests/q20 -q
```

Expect: all green.

## Done when

- [ ] consolidation + contradiction→dimension implemented and tested (no averaging)
- [ ] random + stateless baselines implemented
- [ ] growth dashboard renders `results/phase-2/growth.md`

## If stuck

`plan/30-phases/phase-2-20questions/game-spec.md` (learning loop), `plan/30-phases/phase-2-20questions/experiments.md` → E2.2/E2.5.

"""Post-game learning: consolidation + contradiction -> dimension (step 15).

Learning here never touches neural weights. Game answers become
assertions with mandatory provenance; verification against the existing
CODEX promotes / disputes / keeps them; a repeated ``sometimes`` or a
genuine conflict becomes a NEW context TERM (invariant #6: contradiction
drives ontology expansion) and the conflicting assertions are re-expressed
under distinct contexts — never averaged.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

from kainos.codex.models import (
    Assertion,
    Context,
    EpistemicState,
    ExceptionState,
    Provenance,
    Source,
    TermRef,
)
from kainos.q20.seed import HAS_PROPERTY, IS_A

__all__ = ["consolidate", "detect_dimension", "DECLARES_DIMENSION", "DIM_KIND"]

DECLARES_DIMENSION = "declares_dimension"
DIM_KIND = "dimension"


def _game_provenance(game_id: str) -> Provenance:
    return Provenance(source=Source(uri=f"game_{game_id}", version="1"), observer="oracle", verified=False)


def _dimension_id(property: str) -> str:
    return f"dim:{property}"


def _load_question(question_id: str) -> dict:
    records = json.loads(Path("data/q20/questions.json").read_text())
    for q in records:
        if q["id"] == question_id:
            return q
    raise KeyError(f"unknown question id: {question_id!r}")


def consolidate(target: str, trace: list[dict], codex, game_id: str = "g1", corpus: list[dict] | None = None) -> dict:
    """Turn one game's (question, answer) trace into CODEX assertions.

    Each row becomes an assertion by ``target``:
      property_probe            -> target --has_property--> "<prop>=<answer>"
      category_probe yes/no     -> target --is_a--> category (polarity False for 'no')
    ``unknown`` answers are SKIPPED (absence is the signal — we never write
    'unknown' assertions).

    Verification against existing assertions:
      same value, existing established -> new one promoted to established;
      same value otherwise             -> new one stays candidate;
      conflicting value & one side established -> BOTH become disputed,
        evidence-linked, exception=conflicting (kept, never dropped).
    """

    label = target
    if corpus:
        for c in corpus:
            if c["id"] == target:
                label = c["label"]
                break
    subject = TermRef(id=target, labels=[label])
    stats = {"game_id": game_id, "processed": 0, "promoted": 0, "disputed_pairs": 0, "kept_candidate": 0, "skipped_unknown": 0}
    for i, row in enumerate(trace):
        qid = row["question"]
        answer = row["answer"]
        if answer == "unknown":
            stats["skipped_unknown"] += 1
            continue
        stats["processed"] += 1
        q = _load_question(qid)
        a_id = f"as_{game_id}_{i}_{qid}"
        if q["kind"] == "property_probe":
            assertion = Assertion(
                id=a_id,
                subject=subject,
                relation=TermRef(id=HAS_PROPERTY),
                object=f"{q['property']}={answer}",
                status=EpistemicState.candidate,
                provenance=_game_provenance(game_id),
            )
        else:
            assertion = Assertion(
                id=a_id,
                subject=subject,
                relation=TermRef(id=IS_A),
                object=TermRef(id=q["category"], labels=[q["category"]]),
                polarity=answer == "yes",
                status=EpistemicState.candidate,
                provenance=_game_provenance(game_id),
            )
        codex.add(assertion)
        verdict = _verify(assertion, codex)
        if verdict == "promoted":
            stats["promoted"] += 1
        elif verdict == "disputed":
            stats["disputed_pairs"] += 1
        else:
            stats["kept_candidate"] += 1
    return stats


def _verify(new: Assertion, codex) -> str:
    """Compare one fresh assertion against its existing siblings. Returns
    'promoted' | 'disputed' | 'kept'."""

    new_val = new.object if isinstance(new.object, str) else new.object.id
    existing = codex.query(subject=new.subject.id, relation=new.relation.id)
    matched: list[Assertion] = []
    for a in existing:
        a_val = a.object if isinstance(a.object, str) else a.object.id
        same_object = a_val == new_val
        if same_object and a.relation.id == IS_A:
            if a.polarity != new.polarity:
                same_object = False
        if same_object or (new.relation.id == HAS_PROPERTY and a_val.split("=")[0] == new_val.split("=")[0]):
            # property: same property key is 'matched' even for conflicting values
            matched.append(a)
    if not matched:
        return "kept"
    conflict = [a for a in matched if (a.object if isinstance(a.object, str) else a.object.id) != new_val]
    if not conflict and any(a.status == EpistemicState.established for a in matched):
        codex.update_status(new.id, EpistemicState.established)
        return "promoted"
    if conflict and any(a.status == EpistemicState.established for a in conflict):
        for a in conflict:
            codex.update_status(a.id, EpistemicState.disputed, evidence=[new.id])
            existing_obj = codex.get(a.id)
            existing_obj.exception = ExceptionState.conflicting
            codex.add(existing_obj)
        new.exception = ExceptionState.conflicting
        codex.update_status(new.id, EpistemicState.disputed, evidence=[a.id for a in conflict])
        return "disputed"
    return "kept"


def detect_dimension(codex, property: str, game_id: str = "dimension") -> dict | None:
    """Propose the context TERM for ``property`` when it is exceptional.

    Trigger: an established/candidate assertion with value ``sometimes``, or a
    subject carrying >= 2 distinct established values for the property
    (a contradiction). Registers ``dim:<property>`` via a
    ``<property> --declares_dimension--> dim:<property>`` assertion (the
    dimension is KNOWLEDGE the reasoner can see, not a code comment) and
    re-expresses every implicated assertion under a distinct context
    (``dimension`` + ``value``/``conditional`` + exception=requires_context).
    Never averages: both sides stay, fully distinguished.

    Returns ``{"dimension", "declaration", "reexpressed"}`` or None.
    """

    prefix = f"{property}="
    relevant = [
        a
        for a in codex.query(relation=HAS_PROPERTY)
        if isinstance(a.object, str) and a.object.startswith(prefix)
    ]
    by_subject: dict[str, dict[str, Assertion]] = {}
    sometimes: list[Assertion] = []
    for a in relevant:
        value = a.object.split("=", 1)[1]
        by_subject.setdefault(a.subject.id, {})[value] = a
        if value == "sometimes":
            sometimes.append(a)
    conflicts = {s: vals for s, vals in by_subject.items() if len(vals) > 1}
    if not conflicts and not sometimes:
        return None

    dim_id = _dimension_id(property)
    prop_term = TermRef(id=property, labels=[property], kind="property")
    dim_term = TermRef(id=dim_id, labels=[f"{property} (dimension)"], kind=DIM_KIND)
    decl_id = f"as_{DECLARES_DIMENSION}_{property}"
    if codex._fetch(decl_id) is None:  # noqa: SLF001 — same-package seam for the id check
        codex.add(
            Assertion(
                id=decl_id,
                subject=prop_term,
                relation=TermRef(id=DECLARES_DIMENSION),
                object=dim_term,
                status=EpistemicState.candidate,
                provenance=_game_provenance(game_id),
            )
        )
    reexpressed: list[str] = []
    implicated: list[Assertion] = list(sometimes)
    for value, a in [(v, vals[v]) for vals in conflicts.values() for v in vals]:
        implicated.append(a)
    for a in implicated:
        current = codex.get(a.id)
        value = a.object.split("=", 1)[1]
        data = {"dimension": dim_id, "value": value}
        if value == "sometimes":
            data["conditional"] = True
        current.context = Context(data={**current.context.data, **data})
        current.exception = ExceptionState.requires_context
        codex.add(current)
        reexpressed.append(a.id)
    return {"dimension": dim_id, "declaration": decl_id, "reexpressed": reexpressed}

"""Comparison baselines for the E2 experiments (step 15).

Both expose the policy interface the Game plays through:
``choose(space, oracle) -> question | None``.

- :class:`GreedyIGPolicy` — the pipeline's policy: adaptive info gain
  (step 14). Kept here so policies are comparable in one place.
- :class:`RandomQuestioner` — uniform random valid questions, seeded and
  reproducible, asks each question at most once, then stops (``None``).
- :class:`StatelessGreedy` — IG computed ONCE over the frozen full corpus,
  turning into a fixed question order: it never adapts to the answers it
  receives and ignores everything the CODEX has learned (A1/A3 falsifiers).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

from kainos.q20.hypothesis import HypothesisSpace
from kainos.q20.selector import best_question, expected_information_gain

__all__ = ["GreedyIGPolicy", "RandomQuestioner", "StatelessGreedy"]


class GreedyIGPolicy:
    """Adaptive maximum-information-gain selection (the pipeline's policy)."""

    def __init__(self, questions: list[dict], cost: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> None:
        self.questions = questions
        self.cost = cost

    def choose(self, space: HypothesisSpace, oracle) -> dict | None:
        if len(space) <= 1:
            return None
        question, _ = best_question(space, self.questions, oracle, self.cost)
        return question


class RandomQuestioner:
    """Uniformly random VALID questions, seeded: reproducible per seed.

    Each question is asked at most once (shuffled deck); ``choose`` returns
    ``None`` when the deck is exhausted — the game then guesses.
    """

    def __init__(self, questions: list[dict], seed: int = 0) -> None:
        self.seed = seed
        self._deck = list(questions)
        random.Random(seed).shuffle(self._deck)
        self._i = 0

    def choose(self, space: HypothesisSpace, oracle) -> dict | None:
        if self._i >= len(self._deck):
            return None
        q = self._deck[self._i]
        self._i += 1
        return q

    @property
    def order(self) -> list[str]:
        return [q["id"] for q in self._deck]


class StatelessGreedy:
    """IG selection over the FROZEN corpus: a fixed questionnaire.

    IGs are computed once on the full (unfiltered) space, so every game
    plays the same question order regardless of the answers observed or
    what the CODEX has since learned. The meaningful A1/A3 baseline:
    'smart questions, no learning'.
    """

    def __init__(self, questions: list[dict], oracle, all_ids: set[str] | list[str], cost: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> None:
        space = HypothesisSpace(set(all_ids))
        stats = {q["id"]: expected_information_gain(space, oracle, q, cost) for q in questions}
        self._order = sorted(questions, key=lambda q: (-stats[q["id"]]["ig"], stats[q["id"]]["unknown"], stats[q["id"]]["cost"]))
        self._i = 0

    def choose(self, space: HypothesisSpace, oracle) -> dict | None:
        if self._i >= len(self._order):
            return None
        q = self._order[self._i]
        self._i += 1
        return q

    @property
    def order(self) -> list[str]:
        return [q["id"] for q in self._order]
